content:
maya (Design): quick accessibility pass on the new dashboard filter chips. noticed keyboard users can't tell which chip group has focus when tabbing. visual is a faint underline only. screenshot: https://img.redwood/filters/chips.png :mag:
zane (Frontend): are these the compact chips in the filter bar? we render them as button elements inside a scroll container. current focus style is `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` which is too subtle in dark theme.
maya (Design): exactly. also contrast between selected chip text and bg in dark mode is borderline (~3.2:1). small text.
ida (A11y): for chip buttons we should ensure focus is perceivable: use an outline with >=3px width and color meeting 3:1 against the chip bg per WCAG's focus contrast guidance. For small text, the color contrast needs 4.5:1 if the chip indicates a state (selected). If it's non-essential, we can add aria-pressed to indicate selected.
zane (Frontend): current CSS: ```css
.chip { background: #1f2226; color: #c8cbd1; padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: 16px; font-size: 12px; }
.chip:focus { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.15); }
.chip[aria-pressed="true"] { background: #2b2f36; }
```
ida (A11y): I recommend: - selected chip bg -> #34383f with text #ffffff (contrast ~6.5:1) - focus outline -> 3px solid var(--accent-400) with outline-offset: 2px - add `aria-pressed` on toggle chips and `aria-label` describing the filter when truncated (we have a lot of truncation on small screens).
maya (Design): sounds good. can we also ensure the scroll container has keyboard arrows shortcuts? left/right arrows should move between chips when focused. Mobile remains touch.
zane (Frontend): implement arrow key handling with roving tabindex pattern: only the focused chip has tabindex=0 others -1. JS snippet: ```js
chips.forEach((c,i)=>{ c.tabIndex = i===0?0:-1; c.addEventListener('keydown', (e)=>{ if(e.key==='ArrowRight') focusNext(i); if(e.key==='ArrowLeft') focusPrev(i); }); });
```
ida (A11y): roving tabindex is good. make sure screen reader users still get the pressed state announced. aria-pressed toggles on space/enter and we update `aria-label` to include the count like "Language: Python, 12 results" when filters apply.
tom (QA): add tests: keyboard: tab to chip bar, arrow to move, space toggles pressed state and visually selected; focus ring visible in both themes; truncated chip uses full aria-label. Matrix: VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS.
ci-bot: accessibility-lint: chips-contrast (low), chips-focus-visibility (medium). link: https://ci.redwood/a11y/2295559012
maya (Design): small copy nit: for `aria-label` include context: "Filter: Language, Python (12)" rather than just the value. helps SR users.
ida (A11y): agree. Also debounce the announcement of counts so rapid toggles don't spam. Use `aria-live="polite"` region for that.
zane (Frontend): estimate 2 dev hours: update CSS vars, add roving tabindex, aria-label changes, and unit tests for keyboard behavior. I'll open a PR and tag you both.
maya (Design): thanks. leaving color final to frontend once they run contrast tool.
ida (A11y): i'll review the PR and verify NVDA + VoiceOver passes.
zane (Frontend): PR -> https://git.redwood/pr/7999 (WIP). preview -> https://deploy-preview.redwood/7999
tom (QA): i'll queue passes for tomorrow.
maya (Design): thanks all :raised_hands:
ci-bot: created ticket INFR-423 for follow-up (chip truncation analytics).
